items.title: Al Gafa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2023
items.q: And the other influence on me was Wes Montgomery... I think he was a more influential on my career than Johnny Smith

ctx.x: I think I read that Johnny Smith was an influence on you when you first started playing. Is that correct?

Yeah it was. I loved the sound that he got, I loved the voicings that he got, and I wanted to try to figure out how to do both. The technique I could do, the voicings, my fingers were not as long as his were and not — yeah. I worked — I got one part of it but not both parts. And so I used to listen to him so much that if I bought a new album I could tell you what he was going to play before he even played it, and where he was going to play. I © Fillius Jazz Archive -19-

could just hear it you know. He was definitely an influence in that part of my career. But the other influence on me was Wes Montgomery. I used to go to, there was a club in Harlem called “Count Basie’s.” They used to feature guitar trios: guitar, organ and drums. And it was loaded with really good players, Wes, Kenny Burrell, Grant Green, George Benson, and a saxophone player named Eddie Harris. So I go in to listen to Wes and I’d listen from ten to two in the morning. Then I’d drive home and I’d practice…
